Record Class SlotRef

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.menukit.api.window.SlotRef
Record Components:
container - the container the slot reads and writes
containerSlot - the slot's index within container
slot - the live slot on the menu, or null off-menu
menu - the open menu, or null off-menu
player - who is acting, or null for automation
category - the slot's category on menu, or null when off-menu or in no category
address - the slot's window address, or null when the seam cannot identify the container
public record SlotRef(net.minecraft.world.Container container, int containerSlot, @Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot, @Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu, @Nullable net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, @Nullable SlotGroupCategory category, @Nullable Address address) extends Record
The slot an operation is about to act on, as much of it as the seam can supply. What a SlotOperations.Veto sees.

Every seam has the backing Container and the container-relative index, which is how a locking mod already keys its locks (the player inventory by index, an ender chest by index, a placed container by identity). A menu seam also has the live Slot and its menu, and from those the slot's SlotGroupCategory on that menu. A click seam has the acting Player; a per-player lock needs to know whose click this is, so a LAN guest is not checked against the host's locks. The slot's Address is here too, minted once by the installed rule, so a veto that keys on it never derives it itself. Anything the seam does not have is null: an inventory insert (Inventory.getFreeSlot) has no menu and no slot, only the inventory, its index and its owner, and an address only where the container has an identity.
